title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields
description:
S01 E06 — After Antietam: Photography and Medicine
The war photographers provide an up-close look at the devastation caused during the Antietam battle. Compassionate medics like Clara Barton go down in history as heroes.

title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields
description:
S01 E07 — The Battle of Fredericksburg
The politically driven decision to replace McClellan with Burnside leads the Union soldiers to their doom in Fredericksburg.

title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields
description:
S01 E08 — The Battle of Chancellorsville
Victory comes at a heavy price for Robert E. Lee in the Battle of Chancellorsville after he employs some arguably high-risk battle strategies.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E01 — Andrée de Jongh and the Resistance
When the Germans begin their rapid invasions across Europe, many ordinary citizens are stunned; Dedee de Jongh, a 23-year-old nurse, builds an escape line through Belgium and France to rescue stranded British airmen; her courage and ingenuity.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E02 — The Tory Rebels Who Helped Save England
In hindsight, it may appear inevitable that Winston Churchill takes command; at the time, it seems unthinkable that Neville Chamberlain steps down; how a few brave politicians orchestrate one of the most striking political transitions in history.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E03 — Victor de Laveleye and V for Victory
As an Olympic athlete, Victor de Laveleye is not an ordinary man; there is no reason to think he comes up with one of the war's most popular symbols, helping to buoy spirits and wage psychological warfare; the story of the V for Victory campaign.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E04 — Wilhelmina and Haakon: Royalty Fight Back
When the Germans invade the Netherlands and Norway, Adolf Hitler wants to secure the leadership of these nations; the wrenching decisions and harrowing escapes of Queen Wilhelmina and King Haakon; how these royal figures fight the war from Britain.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E05 — Polish Pilots and the Battle of Britain
The RAF's air battle to defend Britain from Germany in 1940; few people know that roughly 20 percent of the RAF consists of non-British pilots; witnessing the courage and successful maneuvers of Polish fighter pilots who save the day.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E06 — Wendell Willkie: "A Godsend to This Country"
It might seem impossible to find a politician willing to sabotage his own campaign; that is exactly what Wendell Willkie does in his 1940 run against President Roosevelt: why he goes against his own party and supports FDR's plans to help Britain.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E07 — The Earl of Suffolk and Heavy Water
Charles Henry George Howard, the 20th Earl of Suffolk, is an Englishman who seems unlikely to be responsible for the future of the free world; how he smuggles French scientists to England; how he foils Nazi efforts to obtain a nuclear bomb.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E08 — Marie-Madeleine Fourcade: Spymaster
For years, the history books suggest there are no women leaders of the Resistance in France; the story of Marie-Madeleine Fourcade blows this theory out of the water; meeting this extraordinary woman; how she leads a spy ring throughout France.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E01 — America Enters the War
U.S. Marines arrive in June 1965 to protect a U.S. air base; the North Vietnamese Army and the southern Viet Cong guerrillas launch attacks.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E02 — French Indochina and the Viet Minh
Surveying the economic exploitation and repression that defines Vietnam in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E03 — Dien Bien Phu and Vietnam Divided, 1953-1959
Examining mid-century Vietnam from the First Indochina War to the October 1955 referendum.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E04 — Five Leaders Who Defined the Vietnam War
Explore the makings of war in Vietnam through five major players, starting with Vietnamese leaders Hồ Chí Minh and Lê Duẩn in the north and Ngo Dinh Diem in the south.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E05 — The Rise of the Viet Cong, 1959-1962
Examining why the northern Vietnamese government decided to wage guerilla war in the south, and how it's adversaries responded.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E06 — South Vietnam in Crisis, 1963
In 1963, South Vietnam careens toward crisis; exploring the ARVN's deficiencies from lackluster military commanders to political legitimacy.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E07 — The Gulf of Tonkin and a Crossroads, 1964
Examining how the specter of communism in neighboring Indonesia shaped calculations made by the United States.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E08 — The Vietnam War in the Skies
While the United States boasts an impressive air force, its air campaign struggles when confronted by VC forces.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E01 — America: Forged in War
Exploring The French and Indian War of the mid-1700s, which is one of the formative conflicts in American military history; focusing on the experiences of Lt. Col. George Washington, a young colonial officer fighting for the British.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E02 — George Washington Takes Command
When the colonies begin their struggle for independence, they choose George Washington to lead the army; Washington's defense of Boston; his defeat trying to hold New York City; contrasting British and American objectives in the Revolutionary War.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E03 — Redcoats Fall to the Continental Army
Washington's army is in dire straits; his command is in question; he revives his reputation with the famous crossing of the Delaware River; the next four years of the American Revolution, which see Britain's strategic advantage deteriorate.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E04 — Andrew Jackson and the War of 1812
Why the United States chooses to fight Britain in the War of 1812; America's grievances and ambitions, which include the conquest of Canada; the poor strategy, command and training that lead to a strategic stalemate; the exception is Andrew Jackson.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E05 — The Mexican-American War of 1846-1848
The continental U.S. reaches its present span due to the Mexican-American War; the strategies and tactics of generals Zachary Taylor and Winfield Scott; what disciplined and bold maneuvers conducted by a professional army can accomplish.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E06 — Opening Volleys of the Civil War: 1861-1862
The Civil War sets the pattern for warfare in the 20th and 21st centuries; the political events leading up to the war; the strategy devised by Winfield Scott; the chaotic First Battle of Bull Run; developments in the western theater.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E07 — The Civil War's Main Front: 1862
The ebb and flow of battle in the eastern theater; President Lincoln promotes and fires top commanders; The South faces instability in its top ranks until Robert E. Lee becomes the Rebel army's leader; following events through the Battle of Antietam.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E08 — Vicksburg to Gettysburg: 1862-1863
In the summer of 1863, the Civil War reaches a climax on two fronts; studying the generalship of Grant in isolating and defeating the Confederate force defending Vicksburg; dissecting Gen. George Meade's tactics that halt Lee's invasion of the North.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E01 — What is a Pirate?
Exploring the reasons piracy endures from ancient times until today; why it is so difficult to both define and eradicate; how one can understand the rule of law and the rights of nations and individuals on the high seas and in borderless realms.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E02 — Pirate Facts and Fictions
Examining popular pirate legends; discovering which aspects include some truth and which contain none at all; pirate literature can teach a lot about the Jolly Roger, gold-filled treasure chests, the pirate Edward Thatch and more.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E03 — Real Pirates of the Caribbean
How the Spanish's power hold on the Caribbean is broken; which nationalities join in the free-for-all; the historical importance of Alexander Exquemelin's "Buccaneers of America" and Captain Charles Johnson's "A General History of the Pyrates".

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E04 — Pirate Attacks and Tactics
Pirates want money or anything they can turn into money; consequently, they usually wish for a speedy surrender, do not want a battle and rarely sink captured ships; the many tactics pirates use to apprehend their prey in the age of sails.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E05 — Buried Treasure and Pirate Economics
Very few pirates hit it big or try to bury their treasure on a deserted island; exploring the business aspect of piracy, which is one of the few aspects of life pirates can control; piracy is a no-prey, no-pay system; the risk of no pay is very real.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E01 — Westward the Course of Empire
Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E02 — The West in the Colonial Era
Understanding the mark left on the American West by its earliest colonists; the Spaniards, who introduce horses; the French, who develop a complex trade system; the English, who have little interest in colonizing the west of the Appalachians.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E03 — Venturing Beyond the Appalachians
After the Revolutionary War, the land between the Appalachians and the Mississippi becomes part of the new republic; how the territory is organized; the Northwest Ordinance of 1787 creates a new set of rules that clashes with old realities.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E04 — Discoveries of Lewis and Clark
The journey of the two explorers who map the Louisiana Purchase between 1804 and 1806; how Lewis and Clark fit into the tradition of explorers looking for a water route to the Pacific; the political and geographic history of the Louisiana Purchase.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E05 — The Fur Trade and the Mountain Men
Fur traders and mountain men play an integral part in exploring and mapping the American West; why fur is a precious commodity; how John Jacob Astor dominates the American fur trade; how famous mountaineers like Jedediah Smith become legends.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E06 — Trail of Tears
One of the most dismal episodes in the story of the American West; the forced migration of the "Five Civilized Tribes" under the Indian Removal Act of 1830; it is this ordeal that the Cherokee come to call the "Trail of Tears".

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E01 — Julia Disobeys Emperor Augustus
The experiences of Julia, the daughter of Caesar Augustus; a window into the way many pre-modern societies sought to control morality; Julia's life of thwarted potential; understanding what women had to overcome to make a mark on history.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E02 — Herodias Has John the Baptist Beheaded
The portrayal of the John the Baptist's death as the whim of the young femme fatale Salome; why the truth is much more complicated; the story of Salome's mother, Herodias; how Herodias's hunger for power and recognition left her exiled and forgotten.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E03 — The Trung Sisters of Vietnam Fight the Han
China under the Han Dynasty; how imperial expansion threatened the matriarchal culture of Vietnam; the Trung sisters; leading tribal armies against the invaders; how the Trung sisters' story has become a touchstone of Vietnamese culture.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E04 — Boudicca Attacks the Romans
The end of Iron Age Britain and the birth of Roman Britain; the valiant but thwarted rebellion of the Celtic warrior queen, Boudicca; how Boudicca was motivated by personal tragedy; the revival of Boudicca's legacy by Queen Victoria.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E05 — Poppaea Helps Nero Persecute Christians
Nero's reputation for excess and cruelty; how Poppaea became the wife of the mad emperor; how Poppaea's religious sympathies likely influenced Nero's persecution of Christians; a complex story of spiritual zeal and vicious cruelty.
